entities.name: Şehzade Korkut
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Şehzade Korkut (died March 13, 1513) was an Ottoman prince, intellectual, and temporary regent whose life and tragic end illuminate the brutal realities of Ottoman imperial succession during the early 16th century. As the eldest surviving son of Sultan Bayezid II, Korkut was a prominent figure in the dynastic struggles that defined the end of his father's reign and the ascension of his younger brother, Selim I. His significance lies not only in his brief political aspirations but also in his considerable scholarly contributions, marking him as a prince of letters in an era often characterized by military prowess.

Born to Bayezid II, Korkut received a comprehensive education befitting an Ottoman prince, excelling in Islamic theology, law, philosophy, and poetry. He served as the governor of several key Anatolian provinces, including Antalya, a traditional training ground for future sultans. In 1509, during a period of his father's ill health, Korkut briefly acted as regent in Constantinople, a testament to his perceived legitimacy and administrative capabilities. However, his political ambitions were ultimately overshadowed by the more ruthless and militarily adept Selim, who actively sought to depose their father and eliminate all rivals to the throne, as per the Ottoman custom of fratricide to prevent civil war.

Korkut initially withdrew from the succession struggle, even attempting a pilgrimage to Egypt to escape the escalating conflict. However, after his father's deposition in 1512 and Selim I's subsequent ascension, Korkut made a final, ill-fated attempt to rally support in Anatolia, presenting himself as a more just and scholarly alternative to his bellicose brother. This challenge was swiftly crushed by Selim's forces, leading to Korkut's capture and execution near Bursa on March 13, 1513. His death solidified Selim I's undisputed control over the Ottoman Empire, paving the way for Selim's aggressive expansionist policies.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Şehzade Korkut's role as a scholarly prince and a contender for the Ottoman throne, whose execution in 1513 solidified Selim I's rule, highlights the brutal mechanisms of imperial succession and the intersection of intellect and power within the Ottoman court.
